sections.html:
Sitting beside Davenport on the Mississippi, Bettendorf faces Moline, East Moline and Rock Island, Illinois, across the water. It counts among the five Quad Cities. The 2020 census counted 39,102 residents, up from 33,217 in 2010, and the city ranks 15th in Iowa. The median age was 39.9.

Property in the city is assessed by the Scott County Assessor, because only Davenport runs its own assessor. The deed goes to the Scott County Recorder.

Your address decides which of two districts serves the house, so look it up before you tell a buyer.

DistrictArea covered
Bettendorf Community School DistrictMost of central, northern and western Bettendorf; operates Bettendorf High School
Pleasant Valley Community School DistrictEastern Bettendorf, plus Pleasant Valley, Riverdale and LeClaire

Edison Academy is a consortium alternative high school in downtown Bettendorf. Private schools include Rivermont Collegiate, Lourdes Catholic School and Morning Star Academy.

The city lies along the river and sees frequent flooding and annual stormwater runoff. A 2000 study of 14 drainageways found 169 inlets inadequate for heavy rainfall, and Crow, Pigeon and Spencer creeks were named as problem areas.

  • Near one of those creeks? Buyers will ask about basement water.
  • Save receipts for any sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing work.
  • Get the flood zone designation from your insurer ahead of listing.

A cash buyer takes the house in its present condition, wet basement included. That spares you a repair that a lender-financed buyer would ask you to make first.

Getting around is another selling point. The I-74 Bridge connects Bettendorf to Moline, Illinois, and a $1.2 billion replacement project that began in July 2017 was completed in 2021.

Landlords in Bettendorf must hold a current rental registration and pass a rental inspection before renting residential property. Registration is filed with the City Clerk first, using the city's online form, and only then can an inspection be booked.

An inspection certificate is issued once the structure is found to comply with the city code. To schedule, email CodeEnforcement@bettendorf.org or call the code enforcement hotline at (563) 344-4064 and leave a message. City Hall is at 1609 State Street, Bettendorf, IA 52722, and the main number is (563) 344-4000.

Before closing, call the city for the inspection cycle, the fees and how registration is handled at a sale, or read the rental housing code yourself. If the house is rented, say so when you first contact us, and we will check what the city expects.

sections.h2: Paying property tax in Scott County
sections.html:
The Scott County Treasurer collects Bettendorf's property tax in two equal parts, due September 30 and March 31, after certifying taxes in July or August.

The Treasurer has two offices in Davenport: the Administrative Center at 600 W. 4th St. and the General Store at 902 W. Kimberly Rd., Suite 6D. Online, an e-check costs $0.25 and a credit card costs 2.25%. At the counter, cash and checks carry no fee, and debit cards cost $2.00 per transaction. Interest starts the first business day after a due date.

Unpaid taxes appear in a June publication and go to the tax sale on the third Monday of June. An open installment can be cleared at closing, though you should request a payoff figure well before the publication date.

sections.h2: What to prepare before asking for an offer
sections.html:
A few facts on hand let the first conversation end with a clear next step.

  • The school district for your address, since two districts split the city.
  • Distance to Crow, Pigeon or Spencer creek, and any history of water in the basement.
  • Rental status, with the registration and inspection certificate if the house is rented.
  • Which tax installments are paid and which are still open.
  • The deed names and any mortgage payoff.

With those answers, the title company can tell us quickly whether the closing can be set for a date that suits you.

A house with tenants needs attention to the city registration and to the lease. Check that the registration is current at the City Clerk and dig out your inspection certificate. Buyers and title companies may want both, and a missing certificate is easier to chase down early than at the closing table.

Then tell us the lease end date. It decides when a buyer can take possession. Call the code enforcement hotline early and ask what the city wants from you on a sale, since the rules for a change of owner are worth confirming rather than assuming. Keep copies of every notice you receive, in case the buyer wants to see them. Ask the buyer or title company early what paperwork they want, so you are not hunting for it in the last week before closing.

sections.h2: Selling a house with water problems
sections.html:
Water in the basement does not make a house unsellable, but it narrows the field of buyers. Someone with a mortgage usually sends an inspector and an appraiser down there, and repair requests often follow. Someone buying for cash as-is looks at the same house and prices it as it stands.

Whatever route you take, gather what you have: receipts for a sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing, the flood zone designation from your insurer, and any notes about when water got in. Being open about it up front is better than having a buyer discover it, and it keeps the closing from stalling over a surprise.

After you accept an offer, the title company verifies the owners and looks for anything attached to the house, such as a mortgage, a lien or an unpaid tax installment. Nothing needs a lender's approval, so the schedule depends mostly on how quickly those questions get answered.

At the closing you sign the deed and the statements the recorder needs. Open tax and any mortgage payoff are paid from the sale price, and you receive what is left. Because Bettendorf is in Scott County, the paperwork is filed there, and the county Treasurer's record shows whether installments were paid. Ask for a copy of the final settlement statement for your own file. If you have a rental registration, send code enforcement the buyer's details afterward so nothing stays in your name, and keep the confirmation with your records.

sections.h2: What a Bettendorf cash sale looks like
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so closing depends mostly on title work and your schedule.

  • You send the address and the condition of the house.
  • We review it and send a written offer, which you can accept or decline.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value, and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence.
  • The deed goes to the Scott County Recorder, and transfer tax applies to the sale price over $500.

Property tax in Scott County is due in two installments, September 30 and March 31. Any open installment is settled at closing out of the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bettendorf house with a wet basement or other damage?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to repair water damage first. Disclose known issues accurately.
